summary: Meilisearch is a production-grade, open-source search engine written in Rust, built on LMDB with roaring bitmaps for candidate sets and grenad for external sorting. The core `milli` crate implements a full inverted index with position encoding, Levenshtein automata for typo tolerance (1-2 edits), FST-based term dictionaries, and a multi-criterion ranking pipeline (words, typo, proximity, attribute, sort, exactness). It supports hybrid search combining BM25 full-text with HNSW vector search (arroy/hannoy) via local (candle/tokenizers) or remote (OpenAI, HF Hub) embedders. The HTTP server (actix-web) exposes a RESTful API with 10+ official SDKs. Architecture is a monorepo of 24 crates with mimalloc for performance. Active development: 14,533 commits, ~10 core maintainers, monthly releases, 415 commits in last 2 months. Enterprise features (sharding, S3 snapshots) are source-available under BSL 1.1.

findings.description:
- Full-text search with <50ms latency target (search-as-you-type)
- Typo tolerance (1-2 edits) via Levenshtein automata on FST
- Faceted filtering & filtering with complex boolean expressions
- Sorting by any field at query time
- Hybrid search: BM25 + semantic vectors (HNSW via arroy/hannoy)
- Multi-language tokenization (Latin, CJK, Hebrew, Arabic, Thai, Khmer, Vietnamese, etc.)
- Synonyms, stop words, ranking rules customization
- Distinct/deduplication on field
- Geo-search (lat/lng filtering & sorting)
- Multi-tenancy via signed tenant tokens (JWT)
- Document relations (cross-index references)
- Search rules (dynamic pinning/hiding via Rhai scripts)
- Sharding & replication (Enterprise)
- S3 streaming snapshots (Enterprise)
- Conversational search (AI-generated answers grounded in results)
- Personalization (learning-to-rank via user behavior)
- RESTful API with OpenAPI spec; 10+ official SDKs
- Prometheus metrics, structured logging, health checks

apiSurface:
Meilisearch is primarily an HTTP server (actix-web based) exposing a RESTful API. Core SDK interaction is via language-specific clients (Rust, JS, Python, Go, PHP, Ruby, .NET, Swift) that wrap the HTTP API. The internal Rust crate `milli` is the search engine library with public API for:
- `Index::create_or_open()` - LMDB-backed index creation
- `Search` builder pattern - query, filter, offset/limit, sort, distinct, geo, semantic/hybrid search
- `execute_search()` - full-text search with typo tolerance (Levenshtein automata), faceting, sorting
- `execute_vector_search()` - semantic/hybrid search with embedders (candle, hf-hub, openai)
- Document updates via `index.update_documents()` with JSON
- Settings management: filterable attributes, sortable attributes, ranking rules, synonyms, stop words
- Multi-tenancy via tenant tokens (JWT-based)
- Sharding/replication (Enterprise only)
The HTTP API covers: indexes CRUD, documents CRUD (batch), search (POST /indexes/{uid}/search), settings, stats, tasks, snapshots, keys, health.
integrationPoints:
For Veridian pipeline:
1. Playwright scraper → batch JSON documents → Meilisearch HTTP API (`/indexes/{uid}/documents` batch endpoint)
2. Queue (Redis/RabbitMQ) → index-scheduler task queue for async indexing with progress tracking
3. Search: HTTP API `/search` with filter (brand, price range, specs), sort (price, rating), facets (brand, category), hybrid search for semantic queries
4. Matching: Use distinct on product_id for deduplication; filterable attributes for exact spec matching; geo-search for local availability
5. Embeddings: Generate embeddings offline (sentence-transformers) → include in documents → hybrid search at query time
6. Multi-tenancy: tenant tokens per retailer/source for isolation
7. Snapshots for backup/restore of scraped corpus
8. SDKs available for Python/JS/Go/Rust integration
strengthsForVeridian:
- Excellent fit for laptop spec search: faceted filtering (brand, CPU, GPU, RAM, storage), sorting (price, rating), geo-search (local availability), typo tolerance for user queries
- Hybrid search enables semantic queries like "laptop for video editing under $1500" combining specs + natural language
- Batch document API (200 docs/request) fits ETL pipeline from Playwright scrapers
- Multi-tenancy via tenant tokens isolates data per retailer/source
- Distinct on product_id handles duplicate listings across retailers
- Search rules (Rhai) can pin promoted products or hide out-of-stock
- High performance: <50ms p99, horizontal scaling via sharding (Enterprise)
- Rich SDK ecosystem (Python/JS/Go/Rust) for pipeline integration
- Active maintenance, strong community, production-proven at scale
weaknessesForVeridian:
- Enterprise features (sharding, S3 snapshots) require commercial license (BSL 1.1) - Community Edition limited to single node
- Embedding generation not built-in; need separate pipeline (sentence-transformers, OpenAI API) for vectors
- Rhai scripting for search rules adds complexity; learning curve for dynamic pinning
- Large binary (~100MB) and memory usage (LMDB mapsize) - needs capacity planning
- No native SQL/PostgreSQL integration; pure document store
- Versioning: crates not on crates.io, internal crates don't follow SemVer
- Telemetry enabled by default (opt-out) - may need compliance review
- Minimum Rust 1.85+ (per rust-toolchain.toml) - relatively recent toolchain
